primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Transient or chronic incompetence of the lower esophageal sphincter permits reflux of gastric contents into the esophagus, causing heartburn and regurgitation.
vignette: A 42-year-old man has recurrent burning substernal discomfort after large meals that worsens when lying down and improves with antacids. He also reports sour-tasting regurgitation.
distractor_notes: Achalasia causes progressive dysphagia to solids and liquids rather than acid regurgitation after meals.
Stable angina is exertional and relieved by rest rather than antacids and position.
Perforated ulcer causes acute severe peritoneal pain.
Pancreatitis causes severe persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back.
key_expl: Postprandial heartburn and acid regurgitation worsened by recumbency are classic GERD.
objective: Recognize GERD from typical reflux symptoms.

sources.title: GERD
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes GERD as reflux of stomach contents causing heartburn and regurgitation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Excess acid exposure and impaired mucosal defense, commonly from H pylori infection or NSAIDs, produce mucosal ulceration in the duodenum.
vignette: A 39-year-old man has recurrent burning epigastric pain that improves shortly after eating and returns several hours later.
lead: Which anatomic site is most likely affected?
distractor_notes: Distal esophageal disease produces reflux symptoms.
Colonic disease does not cause meal-related epigastric ulcer pain.
Pancreatic disease usually causes persistent back-radiating pain.
Terminal ileal disease is more typical of Crohn disease.
key_expl: Pain relieved by food and recurring hours later is a classic pattern of duodenal ulcer disease.
objective: Relate typical peptic ulcer pain pattern to duodenal location.
clues: pain improves with food then returns

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Accelerated heme breakdown increases bilirubin production beyond hepatic conjugating capacity, raising unconjugated bilirubin without bilirubinuria.
vignette: A patient with brisk intravascular hemolysis develops jaundice. Urinalysis shows no bilirubin.
lead: Which bilirubin fraction is most likely elevated?
distractors: Only urobilinogen without serum bilirubin elevation
distractor_notes: Conjugated bilirubin is water soluble and can appear in urine; it is more typical of cholestasis or hepatocellular excretory dysfunction.
Delta bilirubin is albumin-bound conjugated bilirubin seen with prolonged cholestasis.
Hemolysis increases bilirubin production.
Urobilinogen may rise, but serum unconjugated bilirubin also increases.
key_expl: Hemolysis increases unconjugated bilirubin, which is albumin-bound and not filtered into urine.
objective: Differentiate unconjugated hemolytic jaundice from conjugated hyperbilirubinemia.

sources.title: Bilirubin blood test
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes unconjugated and conjugated bilirubin and their clinical interpretation.

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes increased red-cell destruction and jaundice in hemolytic anemia.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Bile duct obstruction prevents excretion of conjugated bilirubin into the intestine, increasing serum direct bilirubin, bilirubinuria, pale stools, and often alkaline phosphatase.
vignette: A patient with a common bile duct stone has jaundice, dark urine, pale stools, and markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase.
lead: Which bilirubin fraction is expected to predominate in serum?
distractors: No bilirubin because the liver still conjugates normally
distractor_notes: Unconjugated bilirubin predominates when production exceeds conjugation or conjugation is impaired.
Conjugated bilirubin backs up into blood when biliary excretion is blocked.
Methylmalonic acid is unrelated to bilirubin metabolism.
Biliverdin is an intermediate and is not the principal clinical serum pigment.
key_expl: Obstruction after conjugation causes direct bilirubin reflux into blood and urine.
objective: Recognize conjugated hyperbilirubinemia in extrahepatic obstruction.
clues: high alkaline phosphatase with CBD stone

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Luminal obstruction causes appendiceal distention, ischemia, bacterial overgrowth, and inflammation, producing visceral periumbilical pain that localizes to the right lower quadrant when parietal peritoneum is involved.
vignette: A 19-year-old man has anorexia and abdominal pain that began near the umbilicus and migrated to the right lower quadrant, with fever and rebound tenderness.
distractor_notes: Cholecystitis causes right upper quadrant pain and Murphy sign.
Crohn disease is usually chronic and may cause diarrhea and weight loss.
Renal colic radiates from flank to groin and causes hematuria.
Gastroenteritis usually causes diffuse cramping with vomiting or diarrhea rather than migration to McBurney area.
key_expl: Migration from periumbilical visceral pain to localized right lower quadrant tenderness is classic appendicitis.
objective: Recognize the characteristic pain migration of acute appendicitis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Acid entering the duodenum stimulates S cells to release secretin, which increases pancreatic and biliary bicarbonate secretion to neutralize gastric acid.
vignette: Acidic chyme enters the duodenum after a meal.
lead: Which hormone most directly increases pancreatic bicarbonate secretion?
distractor_notes: Gastrin primarily stimulates gastric acid secretion and mucosal growth.
CCK primarily stimulates pancreatic enzyme secretion and gallbladder contraction.
Somatostatin broadly inhibits gastrointestinal hormones and secretions.
Motilin regulates migrating motor complexes during fasting.
key_expl: Secretin is released by duodenal S cells in response to acid and stimulates bicarbonate-rich pancreatic secretion.
objective: Identify secretin as the major hormone driving pancreatic bicarbonate release.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Fat and amino acids in the duodenum stimulate I cells to release CCK, causing gallbladder contraction and pancreatic enzyme secretion.
vignette: A fatty meal enters the duodenum.
lead: Which hormone most directly causes gallbladder contraction?
distractor_notes: Secretin primarily stimulates bicarbonate secretion.
Gastrin stimulates gastric acid secretion.
Ghrelin promotes hunger and growth hormone release.
Somatostatin inhibits many gastrointestinal secretions.
key_expl: CCK released from duodenal and jejunal I cells in response to fat causes gallbladder contraction.
objective: Identify CCK as the mediator of gallbladder contraction after fat ingestion.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Vitamin B12 binds intrinsic factor secreted by gastric parietal cells and the complex is absorbed in the terminal ileum.
vignette: A patient undergoes resection of the terminal ileum for Crohn disease and later develops vitamin B12 deficiency.
lead: Which normal absorptive process has been lost?
correct: Uptake of intrinsic factor-bound vitamin B12
distractors: Absorption of iron in the duodenum
Absorption of glucose in the jejunum only
distractor_notes: Iron absorption occurs mainly in the duodenum.
Glucose absorption occurs throughout proximal small intestine and is not specific to terminal ileum.
Bile acids are synthesized in the liver, though many are reabsorbed in the ileum.
Pepsin is secreted in the stomach and is unrelated to ileal B12 uptake.
key_expl: The terminal ileum is required for absorption of the intrinsic factor-B12 complex.
objective: Localize vitamin B12 absorption to the terminal ileum.
